answer: Delayed Random Audit Assignment.** Each identity joins a grove of candidates, but the scheduler reveals a fresh verifiable random value only after registrations close, assigning auditors from a hidden hollow of unassigned agents. Since the seed cannot be precomputed, attackers cannot position sybils to audit each other. Every identity must then post a crystal-clear work proof within a short window. Mass-registered identities face unpredictable cross-checks, imposing real per-identity labor and delay costs that scale linearly with each fake account.
